---
title: "flexspan showcase"
subtitle: "Every use case, in every output format"
filters:
  - flexspan

flexspan:
  # ── 1. Styled rules: the filter does the formatting ──────────────────────
  - left: "!!"            # text colour, bold
    color: red
    bold: true
  - left: "=="            # background colour
    bg: yellow
  - left: "++"            # several styles at once
    color: "#2e8b57"
    bold: true
  - left: "+-"            # underline
    right: "-+"
    underline: true
  - left: "!-"            # strike-out
    right: "-!"
    strike: true
    color: gray

  - left: "%["            # inline code, like backticks: %[code here]
    right: "]"
    code: true

  # ── 2. Colour chosen in the text ─────────────────────────────────────────
  - left: "-="            # -=text=-(blue)
    right: "=-"
  - left: "-="            # shortcuts sharing the same opening delimiter
    right: "=-r"
    opts: "red, bold"
  - left: "-="
    right: "=-g"
    opts: "green, bold"
  - left: "-="
    right: "=-b"
    opts: "blue, bold"
  - left: "-="
    right: "=-c"
    opts: "aqua, bold"
  - left: "-="
    right: "=-p"
    opts: "purple, bold"
  - left: "-="
    right: "=-o"
    opts: "orange, bold"

  # ── 3. Class + style ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - left: "(("
    right: "))"
    class: note           # CSS hook in HTML, character style in Word
    color: "#1e90ff"
    italic: true

  # ── 4. Named rule: defined separately for each format (see `format:`) ────
  - left: "%%"
    command: badge

  # ── 5. Symbols (`exact`) and fixed content ───────────────────────────────
  - left: "-"
    right: "\\>"
    exact: true
    content: "→"
    color: crimson
    bold: true
  - left: "\\<"
    right: "-"
    exact: true
    content: "←"
    color: crimson
    bold: true
  - left: "("
    right: "!)"
    exact: true
    content: "!"
    color: white
    bg: darkorange
    bold: true
  - left: "[["
    right: "]]"
    content: "REDACTED"
    color: white
    bg: black

  # ── 6. Format blocks: one rule, a different meaning per output format ────
  - left: "("
    right: "*)"
    exact: true
    content: "★"            # every format ...
    color: goldenrod
    latex:                  # ... but LaTeX uses a command: \fstar{}
      command: fstar
      content: ""
      color: ""
    typst:                  # ... Typst another symbol
      content: "✦"
    revealjs:               # ... and slides add a class
      class: slide-star

format:
  html:
    css: showcase.css
    toc: true
  revealjs:
    output-file: showcase-slides.html
    css: showcase.css
    scrollable: true
    smaller: true
  docx:
    reference-doc: showcase-reference.docx
  typst:
    output-file: showcase-typst.pdf
    keep-typ: true
    include-in-header:
      - text: |
          #let badge(..args, body) = {
            let tones = (info: rgb("#1e90ff"), ok: rgb("#2e8b57"), warn: rgb("#d2691e"))
            box(fill: tones.at(args.pos().at(0, default: "info")),
                inset: (x: 4pt), outset: (y: 3pt), radius: 3pt,
                text(fill: white, weight: "bold", body))
          }
  pdf:
    output-file: showcase-latex.pdf
    keep-tex: true
    include-in-header:
      - text: |
          \definecolor{badgeinfo}{HTML}{1E90FF}
          \definecolor{badgeok}{HTML}{2E8B57}
          \definecolor{badgewarn}{HTML}{D2691E}
          \newcommand{\badge}[2][info]{\colorbox{badge#1}{\textcolor{white}{\textbf{#2}}}}
          \newcommand{\fstar}[1]{\textcolor{red}{$\star$}#1}
---

## Quick reference

All the placeholders defined in this document. Each one is shown in detail in
the sections that follow.

| Syntax                      | Purpose                                   | Result                    |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| `!!text!!`                  | text colour: bold red                     | !!text!!                  |
| `==text==`                  | background colour (highlight)             | ==text==                  |
| `++text++`                  | several styles: green and bold            | ++text++                  |
| `+-text-+`                  | underline                                 | +-text-+                  |
| `!-text-!`                  | strike-out, in gray                       | !-text-!                  |
| `%[code here]`              | inline code, same as backticks            | %[code here]              |
| `-=text=-(blue)`            | colour given as an option                 | -=text=-(blue)            |
| `-=text=-(white, bg=navy)`  | colour and background as options          | -=text=-(white, bg=navy)  |
| `-=text=-(#8a2be2, bold)`   | hex colour and a style as options         | -=text=-(#8a2be2, bold)   |
| `-=text=-r`                 | shortcut: bold red                        | -=text=-r                 |
| `-=text=-g`                 | shortcut: bold green                      | -=text=-g                 |
| `-=text=-b`                 | shortcut: bold blue                       | -=text=-b                 |
| `-=text=-c`                 | shortcut: bold aqua                       | -=text=-c                 |
| `-=text=-p`                 | shortcut: bold purple                     | -=text=-p                 |
| `-=text=-o`                 | shortcut: bold orange                     | -=text=-o                 |
| `((text))`                  | class `note` with colour and italic       | ((text))                  |
| `%%text%%`                  | named rule `badge`                        | %%text%%                  |
| `%%text%%(ok)`              | named rule with an option                 | %%text%%(ok)              |
| `%%text%%(warn)`            | named rule with another option            | %%text%%(warn)            |
| `->`                        | symbol: right arrow                       | ->                        |
| `<-`                        | symbol: left arrow                        | <-                        |
| `(!)`                       | symbol: warning mark                      | (!)                       |
| `[[text]]`                  | fixed content replacing the text          | [[text]]                  |
| `[!!text!!]{.skipspan}`     | protected: placeholders left as typed     | [!!text!!]{.skipspan}     |

## Text colour

```markdown
A !!red!! word. **Bold text with a !!red!! word.** *Emphasis with a !!red!! word.*
!!Red text with **bold** and *emphasis* inside.!!
```

A !!red!! word. **Bold text with a !!red!! word.** *Emphasis with a !!red!! word.*
!!Red text with **bold** and *emphasis* inside.!!

## Background, underline, strike-out

```markdown
==Highlighted==, +-underlined-+, !-struck out-! and ++green and bold++.
***Bold emphasis with ==highlight== and +-underline-+.***
```

==Highlighted==, +-underlined-+, !-struck out-! and ++green and bold++.
***Bold emphasis with ==highlight== and +-underline-+.***

## Inline code

`code: true` turns the enclosed text into inline code, exactly like backticks.
The closing delimiter may be a single character.

```markdown
Run %[ls -la] or %[git status --short], then open %[~/.config/app.toml].
It combines with other styles: -=highlighted code=-(code, bg=gold).
```

Run %[ls -la] or %[git status --short], then open %[~/.config/app.toml].
It combines with other styles: -=highlighted code=-(code, bg=gold).

## Colour chosen in the text

Options go in parentheses, right after the closing delimiter.

```markdown
-=green=-(green), -=hex colour=-(#8a2be2), -=white on navy=-(white, bg=navy),
-=bold orange=-(orange, bold), -=underlined teal=-(teal, underline),
-=only a background=-(bg=gold), -=no option, plain text=-.
```

-=green=-(green), -=hex colour=-(#8a2be2), -=white on navy=-(white, bg=navy),
-=bold orange=-(orange, bold), -=underlined teal=-(teal, underline),
-=only a background=-(bg=gold), -=no option, plain text=-.

## Shortcuts: one opening delimiter, several closing ones

```markdown
-=red=-r, -=green=-g, -=blue=-b, -=aqua=-c, -=purple=-p, -=orange=-o,
and an override: -=plain teal=-b(teal).
```

-=red=-r, -=green=-g, -=blue=-b, -=aqua=-c, -=purple=-p, -=orange=-o,
and an override: -=plain teal=-b(teal).

## Nesting

```markdown
!!Red ==red on yellow== red!!, ==yellow !!red on yellow!! yellow==,
++green -=blue inside green=-b green++, **bold !!red ==marked== red!! bold**.
```

!!Red ==red on yellow== red!!, ==yellow !!red on yellow!! yellow==,
++green -=blue inside green=-b green++, **bold !!red ==marked== red!! bold**.

## Headings with !!colour!! and ==highlight==

```markdown
## Headings with !!colour!! and ==highlight==

A [link with a !!red!! word](https://quarto.org), a footnote[^1], H~!!2!!~O, x^!!2!!^,
"quoted !!red!! text", ~~!!red and struck!!~~.
```

A [link with a !!red!! word](https://quarto.org), a footnote[^1], H~!!2!!~O, x^!!2!!^,
"quoted !!red!! text", ~~!!red and struck!!~~.

[^1]: Footnotes work too: !!red!!, ==highlighted==, -=blue=-b.

## Lists, quotes and tables

```markdown
1. First !!red!! item
   - nested ==highlighted== item

> A quotation with -=green=-g words.

| Status          | Meaning          |
|-----------------|------------------|
| !!failed!!      | ==look at this== |
| -=passed=-g     | ++all good++     |
```

1. First !!red!! item
   - nested ==highlighted== item

> A quotation with -=green=-g words.

| Status          | Meaning          |
|-----------------|------------------|
| !!failed!!      | ==look at this== |
| -=passed=-g     | ++all good++     |

## Class + style

`class` adds a CSS class (HTML) or a character style (Word) on top of the style
keys. LaTeX and Typst simply use the style keys.

```markdown
An ((annotated remark)) in the middle of a sentence.
```

An ((annotated remark)) in the middle of a sentence.

## Named rule

`command: badge` hands the text to `\badge` (LaTeX), `#badge` (Typst),
`.badge` (CSS) or the character style `badge` (Word). Each is defined in the
`format:` section of this document.

```markdown
%%default%% %%passed%%(ok) %%careful%%(warn) and a hand-written span: [span]{.badge}
```

%%default%% %%passed%%(ok) %%careful%%(warn) and a hand-written span: [span]{.badge}

## Symbols and fixed content

`exact` rules have no content: the delimiters are typed together. `content`
replaces the enclosed text.

```markdown
Step one -> step two <- step three. (!) Take care. Options still work: ->(navy)

The password is [[hunter2]].
```

Step one -> step two <- step three. (!) Take care. Options still work: ->(navy)

The password is [[hunter2]].

## Format blocks

A rule can hold a block named after an output format (`latex`, `html`,
`typst`, `docx`, `beamer`, `revealjs`). Its keys replace those of the rule in
that format only.

```markdown
A star (*) that is a gold ★ by default, the command `\fstar{}` in LaTeX and
a ✦ in Typst.
```

A star (*) that is a gold ★ by default, the command `\fstar{}` in LaTeX and
a ✦ in Typst.

## Left alone

```markdown
Wow!! Great!! (delimiters glued to a word), `!!code!!`, $a == b$,
[!!protected by a span!!]{.skipspan}, an unclosed !! delimiter.
```

Wow!! Great!! (delimiters glued to a word), `!!code!!`, $a == b$,
[!!protected by a span!!]{.skipspan}, an unclosed !! delimiter.

::: skipspan
A whole block can be protected: !!not red!!, ==not highlighted==.
:::
